title: Cluster inventory & GPU labeling — scratchpad
content:
Purpose: Working notes for a lightweight, queryable cluster inventory & service-discovery pattern that we can use for routing policies and multi-region control plane decisions. Focus: node labels, canonical GPU type taxonomy, health signals and scoring, and how the control plane syncs this across regions.

High-level goals / constraints:
- Single API that services (router, scaler, admission controllers, scheduler-like components) can query for node capabilities and health.
- Low-latency reads for routing decisions (prefer local region, prefer healthy GPUs, fall back to compatible GPU family).
- Eventual consistency across regions acceptable, but stale data should be bounded (TTL + versioning).
- Keep inventory small (per-node metadata rather than full metrics) to avoid high cardinality hot keys. Heavy metrics remain in Prometheus/TSDB.
- Work in both managed-hosted and private deployments. 

Suggested data model (per-node record) — canonical label keys: (keys lowercase, dot/slug format)
- node-id: unique internal id (string)
- provider-id: cloud instance id (if applicable)
- region: us-west1, eu-central1, etc.
- zone: us-west1-a
- env: prod | staging | dev
- pool: gpu-pool-1 (pool name used by autoscaler/placement)
- role: serving | training | infra
- node-lifecycle: active | draining | decommissioned
- cpu-cores: integer (logical CPUs)
- memory_gb: integer
- gpu.count: integer
- gpu.family: a100 | h100 | rtx6000 | t4 (normalized family string)
- gpu.model: NVIDIA A100-SXM-40GB (raw model name)
- gpu.vendor: nvidia | amd | intel
- gpu.memory_gb: integer per GPU (if heterogeneous, list of ints serialized as CSV)
- gpu.driver: 535.x (driver major/minor)
- kube_version: v1.28.x
- kubelet_ready: True | False
- ip_addresses: comma-separated list
- last_heartbeat: 2026-02-15T12:03:24Z
- inventory_version: monotonic increment or UUID
- health_score: 0-100 (see scoring below)
- taints: comma-separated (key=value:NoSchedule)
- labels: freeform label set (for backwards compat)

Label vs. attribute guidance:
- Use labels for long-lived characteristics (gpu.family, region, pool).
- Use attributes/fields for dynamic state (health_score, last_heartbeat, kubelet_ready).
- Keep the set small and predictable — avoid freeform vendor labels except under labels.

Canonical GPU taxonomy (why): We need to support routing that picks a compatible model binary (quantized variant) or falls back to a smaller model. Instead of exact model names, route by gpu.family first, then model details.
Examples (mapping):
- a100 -> A100 series (SXM/PCI variants normalized to a100)
- h100 -> H100 series
- rtx6000 -> RTX A6000 / RTX6000 class
- t4 -> T4 class
Edge cases: mixed GPU types in a node (rare for infra) — represent as gpu.family list and gpu.memory_gb as list. Consumers should prefer homogeneous nodes when requesting multiple GPUs.

Health signals (what to collect into inventory):
- kubelet_ready (boolean) — immediate gate for scheduling/routing
- node.conditions: disk_pressure, memory_pressure, pid_pressure (if any true => degrade)
- gpu_mem_free_pct (derived metric) — sample at inventory push time, not a streaming metric
- gpu_driver_ok (boolean) — compare installed driver vs. required mapping for supported models
- container_runtime_status (ok | degraded)
- last_heartbeat (ts) and heartbeat_age_seconds (derived)
- node_restarts_last_24h (count)
- kernel_oops_recent (boolean) — if host recorded oops in last 24h
- kubelet_version_compat (boolean) — whether kubelet meets minimal compatibility

Health scoring model (proposal):
- Start at 100. Apply weighted penalties:
  - kubelet_ready=false -> score = 0 (hard fail)
  - heartbeat_age > 90s -> -70
  - disk_pressure or memory_pressure -> -40 each (cap so score >= 0)
  - gpu_driver_ok=false -> -50
  - gpu_mem_free_pct < 15% -> -30
  - node_restarts_last_24h >= 3 -> -30
  - kernel_oops_recent true -> -50
- Thresholds for consumers: >=80 = healthy, 50-79 = degraded (soft route with lower priority), <50 = avoid (unless forced/fallback).

Collection & Sync architecture:
Option A — Agent push (preferred):
- Lightweight node-agent (systemd) that collects sparse metadata and posts to central inventory API every 30s with exponential backoff on failures. Collects static labels + occasional dynamic snapshot (gpu mem, driver).
- Agent signs payload with instance cert (mTLS) when talking to control plane. Private deployments can point to local control plane.

Option B — Pull by control plane:
- Centralized poller reaches into each region's API (kube-apiserver) and node exporter endpoints. Works where we cannot run agents, but higher load and network complexity.

Storage & API:
- Inventory service backed by Postgres for durable records + Redis for hot lookups. Each region has a regional inventory with a changefeed to the global catalog.
- API endpoints: GET /nodes?region=us-west1&gpu.family=a100&health_min=80 -> returns node-id list + ip + labels
- Should support label selectors and simple SQL-like filters for routing.

Multi-region considerations:
- Each region publishes its inventory to a global catalog service asynchronously. Catalog contains last_known_at and region_staleness metrics.
- Routing policy decision flow: prefer same-region healthy nodes; if insufficient capacity, try sibling region with matching gpu.family and health_score >= 70; finally, fall back to cross-family compatible models with notice and cost flag.
- Control plane should expose staleness metadata so services can decide whether to accept cross-region results.

Routing integration patterns:
- Router uses inventory API to pick candidate nodes: query by gpu.family, pool and health_score threshold. If router runs in k8s, use an admission hook or custom scheduler that consumes the inventory service.
- For low-latency decisions (e.g., per-request routing in host API), maintain a local read-cache updated by a regional delta feed (pub/sub). Avoid synchronous calls to global catalog in the hot path.

Edge behaviours / fallback rules (examples):
- If requested family unavailable, map request to compatible families (lookup table) and mark response with fallback_family and expected perf_delta.
- If health_score unexpectedly drops under threshold during allocation, the serving process should have a retry/failover policy (can call back into inventory to re-evaluate).

Telemetry & observability:
- Inventory change events should emit metrics: nodes_added, nodes_removed, label_changes, stale_records_count.
- Expose histogram of inventory API latency and distribution of health_score.
- Log all agent publishes and validation failures for forensics.

Security & privacy:
- Agent-auth via mTLS and short-lived certs provisioned by control-plane CA.
- Minimal PII in inventory — don't store user data; strip tags that could contain secrets.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Open: canonical naming for GPU families that covers upcoming HW (Gaudi2, Habana, future Intel accelerators). (Action: PLAT-1423)
- TODO: implement a PoC agent with publishing cadence 30s and a small Postgres schema. (Owner: Ravi, ticket INFRA-330)
- Open: exact scoring weights — run A/B on traffic to tune. Need simulation harness. (Owner: Elena)
- Decide retention policy for old node records and decommission workflow (compacts history).

Useful commands / snippets for agents:
- nvidia-smi query: nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,memory.total,driver_version --format=csv,noheader
- lspci|grep -i nvidia (quick PCI check)
- docker info | jq '.Runtimes' (runtime check)

Appendix: sample inventory JSON record (single-line for clarity):
{"node-id":"i-0abcd1234","region":"us-west1","zone":"us-west1-b","env":"prod","pool":"gpu-serving-1","gpu.count":"8","gpu.family":"a100","gpu.model":"NVIDIA A100-SXM-40GB","gpu.memory_gb":"40,40,40,40,40,40,40,40","kubelet_ready":"True","last_heartbeat":"2026-02-15T12:03:24Z","health_score":"88"}

Notes: This is intentionally opinionated to get something we can iterate on. The next step is a minimal PoC agent + inventory API and a demo router that uses family-based selection and health thresholds.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Ravi: PoC agent skeleton + Postgres schema (INFRA-330)
- [ ] Elena: scoring simulation harness and baseline weights
- [ ] Maya: build README + API contract draft and circulate to serving-runtime and console teams

End of scratchpad.
